name: Recipe Box Anywhere
idea: A free-to-start web recipe box that works on every device and household member for one account, with one-click import of Paprika, Crouton and Recipe Keeper exports.
description: Recipe-manager buyers keep getting burned by per-device purchases (pay again for Android, Windows, a spouse's phone) and by paywalls that cap or lock saved recipes. This is a browser/PWA recipe box with household sharing and read-only share links for non-users, plus drag-and-drop importers that read the proprietary export files of the big native apps entirely client-side. The moat is the file-format importers (Paprika archive, Crouton, Recipe Keeper, plain text/Google Doc paste) and a robust ingredient/step parser, not the CRUD.
web_delivery: Next.js PWA on Vercel hobby; Supabase auth + Postgres with row-level security for household sharing; importers and recipe-scraping parser run in the browser or in a small serverless function reading schema.org Recipe JSON-LD.
why_hard_to_copy: Correct importers for several proprietary export formats plus a tolerant ingredient and step parser (fractions, units, section headings, messy blog markup) take real iteration; a weekend CRUD clone would not read Paprika/Crouton archives or survive messy sources.

signals.summary: Reviewers on Recipe Keeper say the paid account still shows the free tier on a laptop because sync needs a separate purchase per platform (title: "You have to pay for the app separately on each device"). I read about 15 reviews of 1-3 stars since Oct 2025 with the same per-device or no-family-sharing complaint, e.g. 2026-10-15, 2026-09-29, 2026-09-16, 2026-07-27, 2026-06-26, 2026-05-23.
signals.engagement: about 15 of ~56 recent 1-3 star reviews (250 read) repeat this

signals.summary: A Paprika user dropped it for a free notes app because the computer version costs another $30 and notes sync to the web for free; others complain of repurchasing for macOS (2026-08-30) and of lost recipes with no support reply (2026-03-27, 2025-12-23).
signals.engagement: about 6 of 60 recent 1-3 star reviews (250 read)

signals.summary: Pepper users say recipes become inaccessible if the roughly $40/year plan lapses ("It Costs You"), and one calls sharing recipes too expensive (2026-04-03).
Crouton's free tier caps users at 5 recipes before a $20-30 upgrade ("Only 5 recipes"); others say features bought earlier moved behind a monthly fee and there is no bulk import (2026-01-12).

satellite.name: Recipe file converter
satellite.what: Drop a Paprika, Crouton or Recipe Keeper export and get clean Markdown, JSON or printable PDF locally in the browser.
satellite.why_shared: People stuck on a dying or paywalled app want an exit and will share a free tool that frees their recipes.
satellite.handoff: After conversion, a button imports the same file into Recipe Box Anywhere.

where: Mac Power Users and other app-switcher forums
cooking Facebook groups for Paprika users
marketing.target: Home cooks who bought Paprika, Recipe Keeper or Crouton and now use a mix of iPhone, Android and Windows, plus couples sharing one recipe collection
marketing.funnel: Free converter page -> import into the box -> share link to spouse -> household invite
marketing.cold_outreach: Reply in forum threads asking for a cross-platform recipe app with the converter link as the answer
post_ideas: I got tired of paying for the same recipe app four times, so I built a free one
Export your Paprika recipes to Markdown in your browser, nothing uploaded
Why your recipe app should not lock your recipes behind a subscription

capital_note: Domain only; Supabase and Vercel free tiers
notes: Crowded space; moat rests on importers and parser quality and on free hosted sharing. Social-video caption import (Instagram/TikTok) is another recurring gap on Paprika (about 8 reviews, e.g. 2026-10-13, 2026-01-12) but Meta blocks scraping and newer apps (ReciMe, Recipy, Qwikdish) already cover it, so it is a stretch goal, not the core.
